import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 7.41

by Yu. I. Merzlyakov

(John S. Wilson). Is every linear $\overline{SI}$-group an $\overline{SN}$-group?

The classes $\overline{SI}$ and $\overline{SN}$ are Kurosh's classes of generalized solvable
groups. A *system* of subgroups of a group $G$ is a set of subgroups of $G$ that is linearly
ordered by inclusion and *complete*: the union and the intersection of every subset of the
system again belong to the system (in particular the system contains $1$ and $G$). A *jump* of
a system is a pair $A < B$ of its members with no member strictly between them, and the
*factors* of the system are the quotients $B/A$ over its jumps. A system is *normal* if $A$ is
normal in $B$ for every jump $A < B$, and *invariant* if in addition every member is normal in
$G$. A normal (invariant) system is *solvable* if all its factors are abelian. A system
$\mathfrak{B}$ *refines* a system $\mathfrak{A}$ if $\mathfrak{A} \subseteq \mathfrak{B}$.

* $G$ is an $\overline{SN}$-group if every normal system of $G$ can be refined to a solvable
  normal system.
* $G$ is an $\overline{SI}$-group if every invariant system of $G$ can be refined to a solvable
  invariant system.

Systems are arbitrary complete chains of subgroups, not necessarily well-ordered. So these
classes are not the classes $SN^*$ and $SI^*$ (hyperabelian groups) defined by ascending series,
for which the inclusion $SI^* \subseteq SN^*$ is trivial.

A group is *linear* if it is isomorphic to a subgroup of $\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$ for some $n$ and
some field $F$. No restriction is placed on the field or on the group (in particular $G$ need
not be finitely generated).

*References:*
* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46), Problem 7.41
* A. G. Kurosh, *The Theory of Groups*, Vol. II, Chelsea, New York, 1960, Chapter XIV
* D. J. S. Robinson, *Finiteness Conditions and Generalized Soluble Groups*, Part 1,
  Springer, 1972, Chapter 1
-/
namespace Kourovka.«7.41»
universe u
variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

blocks.code:
structure IsCompleteSystem (𝔄 : Set (Subgroup G)) : Prop where
  isChain : IsChain (· ≤ ·) 𝔄
  sSup_mem : ∀ S ⊆ 𝔄, sSup S ∈ 𝔄
  sInf_mem : ∀ S ⊆ 𝔄, sInf S ∈ 𝔄
blocks.docstring:
A *complete system* of subgroups of `G` (Kurosh): a set of subgroups of `G` that is linearly
ordered by inclusion and closed under suprema and infima of all its subsets. For a chain of
subgroups the supremum of a non-empty subset is its union and the infimum is its intersection,
and `sSup ∅ = ⊥`, `sInf ∅ = ⊤`, so a complete system contains `⊥` and `⊤`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib `CompositionSeries` / `RelSeries` (finite only) and `IsAscendingCentralSeries` (ℕ-indexed only); `IsChain` is used as a component.
justification.name: Kourovka.«7.41».IsCompleteSystem
justification.why_needed: Kurosh's complete system of subgroups: a chain of subgroups closed under sSup and sInf of all subsets (hence containing ⊥ and ⊤). Needed as the carrier notion for normal/invariant systems, which may be transfinite and not well-ordered.

blocks.name: IsCompleteSystem
blocks.text:
/-- A *complete system* of subgroups of `G` (Kurosh): a set of subgroups of `G` that is linearly
ordered by inclusion and closed under suprema and infima of all its subsets. For a chain of
subgroups the supremum of a non-empty subset is its union and the infimum is its intersection,
and `sSup ∅ = ⊥`, `sInf ∅ = ⊤`, so a complete system contains `⊥` and `⊤`. -/
structure IsCompleteSystem (𝔄 : Set (Subgroup G)) : Prop where
  isChain : IsChain (· ≤ ·) 𝔄
  sSup_mem : ∀ S ⊆ 𝔄, sSup S ∈ 𝔄
  sInf_mem : ∀ S ⊆ 𝔄, sInf S ∈ 𝔄

blocks.code:
def IsJump (𝔄 : Set (Subgroup G)) (A B : Subgroup G) : Prop :=
  A ∈ 𝔄 ∧ B ∈ 𝔄 ∧ A < B ∧ ∀ C ∈ 𝔄, ¬ (A < C ∧ C < B)
blocks.docstring:
`(A, B)` is a *jump* of the system `𝔄`: `A < B` are members of `𝔄` and no member of `𝔄`
lies strictly between them. The *factor* of the jump is the quotient `B ⧸ A`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `CovBy` (`⋖`), which works on the whole lattice rather than inside the subset 𝔄; using it on the subtype ↥𝔄 was judged less readable.
justification.name: Kourovka.«7.41».IsJump
justification.why_needed: A jump (A, B) of a system: A < B members with no member strictly between; the factors of a system are the quotients over jumps.

blocks.name: IsJump
blocks.text:
/-- `(A, B)` is a *jump* of the system `𝔄`: `A < B` are members of `𝔄` and no member of `𝔄`
lies strictly between them. The *factor* of the jump is the quotient `B ⧸ A`. -/
def IsJump (𝔄 : Set (Subgroup G)) (A B : Subgroup G) : Prop :=
  A ∈ 𝔄 ∧ B ∈ 𝔄 ∧ A < B ∧ ∀ C ∈ 𝔄, ¬ (A < C ∧ C < B)

blocks.code:
structure IsNormalSystem (𝔄 : Set (Subgroup G)) : Prop extends IsCompleteSystem 𝔄 where
  normal_of_isJump : ∀ A B, IsJump 𝔄 A B → (A.subgroupOf B).Normal
blocks.docstring:
A *normal system* of `G` (Kurosh): a complete system in which `A` is a normal subgroup of `B`
for every jump `(A, B)`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: No Mathlib notion of (transfinite) normal series / serial subgroups exists; `Subgroup.Normal` and `Subgroup.subgroupOf` are used as components.
justification.name: Kourovka.«7.41».IsNormalSystem
justification.why_needed: Kurosh's normal system: complete system with A normal in B at every jump.

blocks.name: IsNormalSystem
blocks.text:
/-- A *normal system* of `G` (Kurosh): a complete system in which `A` is a normal subgroup of `B`
for every jump `(A, B)`. -/
structure IsNormalSystem (𝔄 : Set (Subgroup G)) : Prop extends IsCompleteSystem 𝔄 where
  normal_of_isJump : ∀ A B, IsJump 𝔄 A B → (A.subgroupOf B).Normal

blocks.code:
structure IsInvariantSystem (𝔄 : Set (Subgroup G)) : Prop extends IsNormalSystem 𝔄 where
  normal : ∀ A ∈ 𝔄, A.Normal
blocks.docstring:
An *invariant system* of `G` (Kurosh): a normal system all of whose members are normal
subgroups of `G`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Same as above; nothing in Mathlib models chains of normal subgroups with jump structure.
justification.name: Kourovka.«7.41».IsInvariantSystem
justification.why_needed: Kurosh's invariant system: normal system all of whose members are normal in G.

blocks.name: IsInvariantSystem
blocks.text:
/-- An *invariant system* of `G` (Kurosh): a normal system all of whose members are normal
subgroups of `G`. -/
structure IsInvariantSystem (𝔄 : Set (Subgroup G)) : Prop extends IsNormalSystem 𝔄 where
  normal : ∀ A ∈ 𝔄, A.Normal

blocks.code:
def HasAbelianFactors (𝔄 : Set (Subgroup G)) : Prop :=
  ∀ A B, IsJump 𝔄 A B → ⁅B, B⁆ ≤ A
blocks.docstring:
The system `𝔄` has abelian factors: for every jump `(A, B)` of `𝔄` the factor `B ⧸ A` is
abelian, i.e. `⁅B, B⁆ ≤ A`. A normal (invariant) system with abelian factors is a *solvable*
normal (invariant) system in Kurosh's terminology.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `IsSolvable` / `derivedSeries` (finite derived length only) and `IsMulCommutative (B ⧸ A.subgroupOf B)` (requires a Normal instance on the quotient); `Subgroup.commutator` bracket is used instead.
justification.name: Kourovka.«7.41».HasAbelianFactors
justification.why_needed: All factors B/A over jumps are abelian (⁅B, B⁆ ≤ A); this is Kurosh's 'solvable' system when combined with normality.

blocks.name: HasAbelianFactors
blocks.text:
/-- The system `𝔄` has abelian factors: for every jump `(A, B)` of `𝔄` the factor `B ⧸ A` is
abelian, i.e. `⁅B, B⁆ ≤ A`. A normal (invariant) system with abelian factors is a *solvable*
normal (invariant) system in Kurosh's terminology. -/
def HasAbelianFactors (𝔄 : Set (Subgroup G)) : Prop :=
  ∀ A B, IsJump 𝔄 A B → ⁅B, B⁆ ≤ A

blocks.docstring:
`G` is an $\overline{SN}$-group: every normal system of `G` can be refined to a normal system
with abelian factors.

justification.name: Kourovka.«7.41».IsSNBarGroup
justification.why_needed: Kurosh's class SN-bar: every normal system refines to a normal system with abelian factors.

blocks.name: IsSNBarGroup
blocks.text:
/-- `G` is an $\overline{SN}$-group: every normal system of `G` can be refined to a normal system
with abelian factors. -/
def IsSNBarGroup (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ 𝔄 : Set (Subgroup G), IsNormalSystem 𝔄 →
    ∃ 𝔅, 𝔄 ⊆ 𝔅 ∧ IsNormalSystem 𝔅 ∧ HasAbelianFactors 𝔅

blocks.docstring:
`G` is an $\overline{SI}$-group: every invariant system of `G` can be refined to an invariant
system with abelian factors.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `IsSolvable` — not equivalent; no hyperabelian/SI-type class in Mathlib or the repo.
justification.name: Kourovka.«7.41».IsSIBarGroup
justification.why_needed: Kurosh's class SI-bar: every invariant system refines to an invariant system with abelian factors.

blocks.name: IsSIBarGroup
blocks.text:
/-- `G` is an $\overline{SI}$-group: every invariant system of `G` can be refined to an invariant
system with abelian factors. -/
def IsSIBarGroup (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ 𝔄 : Set (Subgroup G), IsInvariantSystem 𝔄 →
    ∃ 𝔅, 𝔄 ⊆ 𝔅 ∧ IsInvariantSystem 𝔅 ∧ HasAbelianFactors 𝔅

blocks.code:
def IsLinearGroup (G : Type u) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (F : Type u) (_ : Field F) (f : G →* GL (Fin n) F), Function.Injective f
blocks.docstring:
`G` is a *linear group*: it is isomorphic to a subgroup of $\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$ for some
`n : ℕ` and some field `F`. Taking `F` in the universe of `G` loses no generality: the subfield
generated by the matrix entries of the image of `G` has cardinality at most `max #G ℵ₀`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup` / `GL` (used as a component); no `IsLinear`-style predicate exists in Mathlib or FormalConjecturesForMathlib (only `diagonalSubgroup` helpers).
justification.name: Kourovka.«7.41».IsLinearGroup
justification.why_needed: A group isomorphic to a subgroup of GL_n(F) for some n and some field F.

blocks.name: IsLinearGroup
blocks.text:
/-- `G` is a *linear group*: it is isomorphic to a subgroup of $\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$ for some
`n : ℕ` and some field `F`. Taking `F` in the universe of `G` loses no generality: the subfield
generated by the matrix entries of the image of `G` has cardinality at most `max #G ℵ₀`. -/
def IsLinearGroup (G : Type u) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (F : Type u) (_ : Field F) (f : G →* GL (Fin n) F), Function.Injective f

  simpa using h.sSup_mem ∅ (Set.empty_subset _)

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isInvariantSystem_pair : IsInvariantSystem ({⊥, ⊤} : Set (Subgroup G)) where
  isChain := by
    rintro A (rfl | rfl) B (rfl | rfl) _
    · exact Or.inl le_rfl
    · exact Or.inl bot_le
    · exact Or.inr bot_le
    · exact Or.inl le_rfl
  sSup_mem S hS := by
    by_cases hT : ⊤ ∈ S
    · exact Or.inr (top_le_iff.mp (le_sSup hT))
    · refine Or.inl (le_bot_iff.mp (sSup_le fun A hA => ?_))
      rcases hS hA with rfl | rfl
      · exact le_rfl
      · exact absurd hA hT
  sInf_mem S hS := by
    by_cases hB : ⊥ ∈ S
    · exact Or.inl (le_bot_iff.mp (sInf_le hB))
    · refine Or.inr (top_le_iff.mp (le_sInf fun A hA => ?_))
      rcases hS hA with rfl | rfl
      · exact absurd hA hB
      · exact le_rfl
  normal_of_isJump A B hAB := by
    rcases hAB.1 with rfl | rfl
    · infer_instance
    · infer_instance
  normal A hA := by
    rcases hA with rfl | rfl
    · infer_instance
    · infer_instance

theorem isSNBarGroup_of_commGroup (G : Type*) [CommGroup G] : IsSNBarGroup G := by

  rw [commutatorElement_eq_one_iff_mul_comm.mpr (mul_comm g₁ g₂)]

claims.decomposer_note: Single unlettered yes/no question, formalizable as answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ G, (G linear, i.e. isomorphic to a subgroup of GL_n(F) for some n and some field F) → G ∈ SI-bar → G ∈ SN-bar; the main subtlety is that the bar classes follow Kurosh's convention (SI-bar: every invariant system — subgroups all normal in G, linearly ordered and complete — can be refined to one with abelian factors; SN-bar: every normal system — each member normal in its successor at every jump — can be refined to one with abelian factors), so these are NOT the 'ascending series' classes SI*/SN* (hyperabelian), and the inclusion SI-bar ⊆ SN-bar is genuinely non-trivial in this reading, whereas it would be trivial under the ascending-series reading; the field is arbitrary (no characteristic or finiteness restriction) and the linear group need not be finitely generated.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same, faithful proposition `answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsLinearGroup G → IsSIBarGroup G → IsSNBarGroup G` with Kurosh-convention definitions (complete chains of subgroups containing ⊥/⊤, normality of A in B at each jump, ⁅B,B⁆ ≤ A for abelian factors, refinement = set inclusion, SI-bar refinements required to be invariant, SN-bar refinements required to be normal; linear = injective hom into GL (Fin n) F for a field F with no restrictions). I verified in Lean that `(A.subgroupOf B).Normal` is exactly 'A ◁ B' for A ≤ B, and that every complete chain has a jump around each nontrivial element (so the abelian-factor condition is never vacuous). c05 chosen as the base for the cleanest definitional layout (separate `IsCompleteSystem`, `extends` structures, `bot_mem`/`top_mem` API lemmas, `{⊥,⊤}` test); I added c07's tests (abelian groups are SN-bar/SI-bar, GL n F is linear) and wrapped two >100-char lines. c04 (CompleteSublattice), c03 (normalizer), c08 (≃* onto a subgroup) are equivalent but less idiomatic.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 7.41

by Yu. I. Merzlyakov

(John S. Wilson). Is every linear $\overline{SI}$-group an $\overline{SN}$-group?

The classes $\overline{SI}$ and $\overline{SN}$ are Kurosh's classes of generalized solvable
groups. A *system* of subgroups of a group $G$ is a set of subgroups of $G$ that is linearly
ordered by inclusion and *complete*: the union and the intersection of every subset of the
system again belong to the system (in particular the system contains $1$ and $G$). A *jump* of
a system is a pair $A < B$ of its members with no member strictly between them, and the
*factors* of the system are the quotients $B/A$ over its jumps. A system is *normal* if $A$ is
normal in $B$ for every jump $A < B$, and *invariant* if in addition every member is normal in
$G$. A normal (invariant) system is *solvable* if all its factors are abelian. A system
$\mathfrak{B}$ *refines* a system $\mathfrak{A}$ if $\mathfrak{A} \subseteq \mathfrak{B}$.

* $G$ is an $\overline{SN}$-group if every normal system of $G$ can be refined to a solvable
  normal system.
* $G$ is an $\overline{SI}$-group if every invariant system of $G$ can be refined to a solvable
  invariant system.

Systems are arbitrary complete chains of subgroups, not necessarily well-ordered. So these
classes are not the classes $SN^*$ and $SI^*$ (hyperabelian groups) defined by ascending series,
for which the inclusion $SI^* \subseteq SN^*$ is trivial.

A group is *linear* if it is isomorphic to a subgroup of $\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$ for some $n$ and
some field $F$. No restriction is placed on the field or on the group (in particular $G$ need
not be finitely generated).

*References:*
* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46), Problem 7.41
* A. G. Kurosh, *The Theory of Groups*, Vol. II, Chelsea, New York, 1960, Chapter XIV
* D. J. S. Robinson, *Finiteness Conditions and Generalized Soluble Groups*, Part 1,
  Springer, 1972, Chapter 1
-/

namespace Kourovka.«7.41»

universe u

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

/-- A *complete system* of subgroups of `G` (Kurosh): a set of subgroups of `G` that is linearly
ordered by inclusion and closed under suprema and infima of all its subsets. For a chain of
subgroups the supremum of a non-empty subset is its union and the infimum is its intersection,
and `sSup ∅ = ⊥`, `sInf ∅ = ⊤`, so a complete system contains `⊥` and `⊤`. -/
structure IsCompleteSystem (𝔄 : Set (Subgroup G)) : Prop where
  isChain : IsChain (· ≤ ·) 𝔄
  sSup_mem : ∀ S ⊆ 𝔄, sSup S ∈ 𝔄
  sInf_mem : ∀ S ⊆ 𝔄, sInf S ∈ 𝔄

/-- `(A, B)` is a *jump* of the system `𝔄`: `A < B` are members of `𝔄` and no member of `𝔄`
lies strictly between them. The *factor* of the jump is the quotient `B ⧸ A`. -/
def IsJump (𝔄 : Set (Subgroup G)) (A B : Subgroup G) : Prop :=
  A ∈ 𝔄 ∧ B ∈ 𝔄 ∧ A < B ∧ ∀ C ∈ 𝔄, ¬ (A < C ∧ C < B)

/-- A *normal system* of `G` (Kurosh): a complete system in which `A` is a normal subgroup of `B`
for every jump `(A, B)`. -/
structure IsNormalSystem (𝔄 : Set (Subgroup G)) : Prop extends IsCompleteSystem 𝔄 where
  normal_of_isJump : ∀ A B, IsJump 𝔄 A B → (A.subgroupOf B).Normal

/-- An *invariant system* of `G` (Kurosh): a normal system all of whose members are normal
subgroups of `G`. -/
structure IsInvariantSystem (𝔄 : Set (Subgroup G)) : Prop extends IsNormalSystem 𝔄 where
  normal : ∀ A ∈ 𝔄, A.Normal

/-- The system `𝔄` has abelian factors: for every jump `(A, B)` of `𝔄` the factor `B ⧸ A` is
abelian, i.e. `⁅B, B⁆ ≤ A`. A normal (invariant) system with abelian factors is a *solvable*
normal (invariant) system in Kurosh's terminology. -/
def HasAbelianFactors (𝔄 : Set (Subgroup G)) : Prop :=
  ∀ A B, IsJump 𝔄 A B → ⁅B, B⁆ ≤ A

/-- `G` is an $\overline{SN}$-group: every normal system of `G` can be refined to a normal system
with abelian factors. -/
def IsSNBarGroup (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ 𝔄 : Set (Subgroup G), IsNormalSystem 𝔄 →
    ∃ 𝔅, 𝔄 ⊆ 𝔅 ∧ IsNormalSystem 𝔅 ∧ HasAbelianFactors 𝔅

/-- `G` is an $\overline{SI}$-group: every invariant system of `G` can be refined to an invariant
system with abelian factors. -/
def IsSIBarGroup (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ 𝔄 : Set (Subgroup G), IsInvariantSystem 𝔄 →
    ∃ 𝔅, 𝔄 ⊆ 𝔅 ∧ IsInvariantSystem 𝔅 ∧ HasAbelianFactors 𝔅

/-- `G` is a *linear group*: it is isomorphic to a subgroup of $\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$ for some
`n : ℕ` and some field `F`. Taking `F` in the universe of `G` loses no generality: the subfield
generated by the matrix entries of the image of `G` has cardinality at most `max #G ℵ₀`. -/
def IsLinearGroup (G : Type u) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (F : Type u) (_ : Field F) (f : G →* GL (Fin n) F), Function.Injective f

/-- A complete system contains the trivial subgroup. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsCompleteSystem.bot_mem {𝔄 : Set (Subgroup G)} (h : IsCompleteSystem 𝔄) :
    ⊥ ∈ 𝔄 := by
  simpa using h.sSup_mem ∅ (Set.empty_subset _)

/-- A complete system contains the whole group. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsCompleteSystem.top_mem {𝔄 : Set (Subgroup G)} (h : IsCompleteSystem 𝔄) :
    ⊤ ∈ 𝔄 := by
  simpa using h.sInf_mem ∅ (Set.empty_subset _)

/-- The two-element system `{⊥, ⊤}` is an invariant system of every group. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isInvariantSystem_pair : IsInvariantSystem ({⊥, ⊤} : Set (Subgroup G)) where
  isChain := by
    rintro A (rfl | rfl) B (rfl | rfl) _
    · exact Or.inl le_rfl
    · exact Or.inl bot_le
    · exact Or.inr bot_le
    · exact Or.inl le_rfl
  sSup_mem S hS := by
    by_cases hT : ⊤ ∈ S
    · exact Or.inr (top_le_iff.mp (le_sSup hT))
    · refine Or.inl (le_bot_iff.mp (sSup_le fun A hA => ?_))
      rcases hS hA with rfl | rfl
      · exact le_rfl
      · exact absurd hA hT
  sInf_mem S hS := by
    by_cases hB : ⊥ ∈ S
    · exact Or.inl (le_bot_iff.mp (sInf_le hB))
    · refine Or.inr (top_le_iff.mp (le_sInf fun A hA => ?_))
      rcases hS hA with rfl | rfl
      · exact absurd hA hB
      · exact le_rfl
  normal_of_isJump A B hAB := by
    rcases hAB.1 with rfl | rfl
    · infer_instance
    · infer_instance
  normal A hA := by
    rcases hA with rfl | rfl
    · infer_instance
    · infer_instance

/-- Every abelian group is an $\overline{SN}$-group: each of its normal systems already has
abelian factors. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isSNBarGroup_of_commGroup (G : Type*) [CommGroup G] : IsSNBarGroup G := by
  intro 𝔄 h𝔄
  refine ⟨𝔄, le_rfl, h𝔄, fun A B _ ↦ ?_⟩
  refine Subgroup.commutator_le.mpr fun g₁ _ g₂ _ ↦ ?_
  rw [commutatorElement_eq_one_iff_mul_comm.mpr (mul_comm g₁ g₂)]
  exact A.one_mem

/-- Every abelian group is an $\overline{SI}$-group: each of its invariant systems already has
abelian factors. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isSIBarGroup_of_commGroup (G : Type*) [CommGroup G] : IsSIBarGroup G := by
  intro 𝔄 h𝔄
  refine ⟨𝔄, le_rfl, h𝔄, fun A B _ ↦ ?_⟩
  refine Subgroup.commutator_le.mpr fun g₁ _ g₂ _ ↦ ?_
  rw [commutatorElement_eq_one_iff_mul_comm.mpr (mul_comm g₁ g₂)]
  exact A.one_mem

/-- The general linear group $\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$ over a field $F$ is a linear group. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isLinearGroup_generalLinearGroup (n : ℕ) (F : Type u) [Field F] :
    IsLinearGroup (GL (Fin n) F) :=
  ⟨n, F, inferInstance, MonoidHom.id _, fun _ _ h ↦ h⟩

/--
(John S. Wilson). Is every linear $\overline{SI}$-group an $\overline{SN}$-group?

Here a group is linear if it is isomorphic to a subgroup of $\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$ for some $n$ and
some field $F$; it is an $\overline{SI}$-group if every invariant system of subgroups can be
refined to an invariant system with abelian factors, and an $\overline{SN}$-group if every normal
system of subgroups can be refined to a normal system with abelian factors (Kurosh).
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«7.41» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsLinearGroup G → IsSIBarGroup G → IsSNBarGroup G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«7.41»

items: SI-bar is read per Kurosh: every invariant system can be refined to a solvable *invariant* system (the refinement must again consist of G-normal subgroups). If a reviewer believes Kurosh/Wilson only require a solvable normal refinement, change `IsInvariantSystem 𝔅` to `IsNormalSystem 𝔅` in `IsSIBarGroup`; under the present reading neither inclusion between SI-bar and SN-bar is trivial, matching the notes.

A 'system' is a chain of subgroups closed under sSup and sInf of *all* subsets (Kurosh's completeness). For a chain, sSup of a non-empty subset is the set-theoretic union (Subgroup.mem_sSup_of_directedOn), and sSup ∅ = ⊥, sInf ∅ = ⊤ encode Kurosh's requirement that the system contain 1 and G. Systems are not required to be well-ordered, so these are not the ascending-series classes SN*/SI*.

A jump is defined directly (A < B in 𝔄 with no member of 𝔄 strictly between) rather than via `CovBy` on the subtype; the factor B/A is never formed as a quotient type. 'B/A abelian' is encoded as ⁅B, B⁆ ≤ A (Subgroup.commutator_le shows this is exactly ∀ x y ∈ B, [x,y] ∈ A), avoiding the need for a Normal instance on the quotient.
'A normal in B' at a jump is `(A.subgroupOf B).Normal`, the standard Mathlib idiom.
Invariant systems are defined as normal systems all of whose members are normal in G (literally Kurosh's definition; the jump-normality clause is then redundant but harmless).
Refinement is set inclusion 𝔄 ⊆ 𝔅 of systems, as in Kurosh.

Linear group: ∃ n : ℕ, ∃ field F, ∃ injective group hom G →* GL (Fin n) F. The field F is taken in the same universe as G (Type u for G : Type u); this loses no generality since the subfield generated by the matrix entries of the image of G has cardinality ≤ max(#G, ℵ₀). No characteristic, finiteness, or finite-generation restriction is imposed, per the notes. The main theorem quantifies over G : Type, following the repository's convention.

Two API lemmas (⊥, ⊤ ∈ every complete system) and one test (the two-element system {⊥, ⊤} is an invariant system of any group) are included with proofs, as CONTRIBUTING.md asks for basic API tests of bespoke definitions.

reviewer_notes: Ambiguity: the notebook uses Kurosh's bar notation without definitions. All candidates and the decomposition table read \overline{SI}/\overline{SN} as Kurosh's classes (Theory of Groups Vol. II, Ch. XIV; also Robinson Part 1, Ch. 1): every invariant (resp. normal) system — a complete chain of subgroups from 1 to G with A normal in B at each jump — can be refined (𝔄 ⊆ 𝔅) to an invariant (resp. normal) system with abelian jump factors. Under this reading SI-bar ⊆ SN-bar is genuinely open (Kurosh/Robinson record it as unknown), matching Wilson's question about the linear case; under the ascending-series (SI*/SN*) reading it would be trivial, so that reading is rejected. A residual uncertainty is whether the SI-bar refinement must itself be invariant (Kurosh's wording, adopted here) or merely a solvable normal system; all eight candidates independently chose the former, and it is the standard definition. Encoding notes: closure under sSup/sInf of *all* subsets encodes Kurosh's completeness plus 1, G ∈ system (sSup ∅ = ⊥, sInf ∅ = ⊤); for a chain, sSup of a nonempty subset is the union (Subgroup.mem_sSup_of_directedOn). The field F is placed in the universe of G (Type), WLOG since the subfield generated by the matrix entries of the image has cardinality ≤ max(ℵ₀, #G). n = 0 is allowed (GL (Fin 0) F trivial) — harmless. The theorem quantifies over G : Type, following existing Kourovka files. No candidate omitted the slot; no decomposition objections were raised. Final file compiles with only the `declaration uses 'sorry'` warning; bespoke definitions are kept in the problem file as in Kourovka/1_40.lean (a maintainer may prefer moving them to FormalConjecturesForMathlib/GroupTheory).
